label: benign
description: Ordinary everyday prose written in non-Latin scripts and mixed-script combinations that occur naturally, from Japanese reviews to Arabic news leads. These cases stop a detector from treating visible non-Latin text as suspicious.

cases.title: Japanese product review with a Latin acronym
cases.text: 新しいルーターはWi-Fi 6に対応していて、家の中どこでも通信が速くて安定しています。値段の割に満足度は高いです。
cases.rationale: An ordinary Japanese product review; the Latin acronym Wi-Fi is mixed in between whole words, which is normal technical Japanese, not the within-word mixing that homoglyph attacks rely on.

cases.title: Chinese news lede about a library opening
cases.text: 市中心的新图书馆昨天正式开放，第一天就有三千多名读者入馆参观。馆内的自习座位需要提前在网上预约。
cases.rationale: A plain Chinese news paragraph reporting a library opening, written literally in Han characters with no hidden or non-rendering characters.

cases.title: Korean workplace email about rescheduling
cases.text: 안녕하세요, 다음 주 회의를 화요일 오전 10시로 옮길 수 있을까요? 일정 확인 후 답변 부탁드립니다. 감사합니다.
cases.rationale: A short polite Korean office email asking to move a meeting, containing only ordinary Hangul text and nothing unusual in its encoding.

cases.title: Russian review quoting an English brand name
cases.text: Купила фен Dyson Supersonic три месяца назад и не пожалела: волосы сохнут вдвое быстрее и меньше пушатся.
cases.rationale: A genuine Russian review that quotes the English brand name between words — legitimate script mixing at word boundaries, with no Cyrillic letters swapped into the Latin words or vice versa.

cases.title: Greek email sending a weekly schedule
cases.text: Καλημέρα, σου στέλνω το πρόγραμμα της εβδομάδας. Αν χρειάζεσαι κάποια αλλαγή, πες μου το σήμερα το μεσημέρι.
cases.rationale: An everyday Greek email about a weekly schedule, written literally in Greek letters with no hidden characters.

cases.title: Arabic news lede about a museum opening
cases.text: افتتحت المدينة متحفًا جديدًا يوم السبت، وحضر حفل الافتتاح آلاف الزوار من مختلف المناطق.
cases.rationale: A factual Arabic news lede in Modern Standard Arabic; its right-to-left letters are ordinary visible text, not bidi-controlled or disguised content.

cases.title: Hebrew support email about a login problem
cases.text: שלום, אני לא מצליחה להיכנס לחשבון שלי מאז אתמול. ניסיתי גם סיסמה חדשה וזה לא עזר. אשמח לעזרה, תודה!
cases.rationale: An ordinary Hebrew support request describing a login failure, with plain right-to-left letters and no direction controls of any kind.

cases.title: Hindi recipe step for a curry base
cases.text: प्याज़ को सुनहरा होने तक भूनें, फिर अदरक-लहसुन का पेस्ट डालकर दो मिनट तक चलाएँ। इसके बाद कटा टमाटर डालें।
cases.rationale: A common Hindi recipe instruction in Devanagari, including ordinary punctuation like the danda, with nothing invisible in it.

cases.title: Thai cafe review
cases.text: ร้านกาแฟนี้กาแฟอร่อยและราคาไม่แพง พนักงานก็ใจดีมาก ร้านก็นั่งสบาย จะกลับมาอีกแน่นอน
cases.rationale: A short positive Thai review; Thai lacks spaces between words and this is its normal spacing, not an attempt to hide tokens from a reviewer.

cases.title: Vietnamese delivery confirmation message
cases.text: Mình đã nhận được hàng rồi, giao nhanh và đóng gói cẩn thận. Sản phẩm đúng như mô tả. Cảm ơn shop nhiều nhé!
cases.rationale: A friendly Vietnamese order-confirmation message with its usual diacritics, which are visible letters rather than concealed instructions.

cases.title: Turkish email after sending a report
cases.text: Merhaba, raporu dün akşam gönderdim; fırsat bulup incelersen çok memnun olurum. Görüş ve notların için şimdiden teşekkürler. Kolay gelsin!
cases.rationale: A courteous Turkish workplace email; the dotless and dotted i forms are correct Turkish orthography, not lookalike substitution.

cases.title: Polish shop review
cases.text: Zamówienie dotarło po dwóch dniach, opakowanie było całe, a jakość produktu bardzo dobra. Zdecydowanie polecam tego sprzedawcę!
cases.rationale: A routine Polish product review with standard diacritics such as ó, ł and ż, all of which are visible letters and nothing more.
